entities.summary: Andalò del Negro was a medieval Italian astronomer and geographer who made significant contributions to the field of astronomy in the 14th century. Born in Italy, del Negro traveled extensively throughout the Mediterranean region, documenting his observations of celestial bodies and geographical features. His work, which included detailed maps of the world and descriptions of astronomical phenomena, was widely studied and admired by scholars of his time. Del Negro's legacy continued to influence astronomical research for centuries, with his works remaining a valuable resource for scholars today. The Andalò del Negro's most notable achievement was his detailed map of the world, which accurately depicted the Earth's circumference and included a detailed description of the stars and constellations. This map, which was widely disseminated throughout Europe, played a significant role in the development of modern cartography and astronomy. Del Negro's contributions to astronomy and geography also had a lasting impact on the scientific community, with his work influencing prominent scholars of the time, including the famous astronomer, Giovanni Domenico Cassini. The Andalò del Negro's significance in the history of astronomy and geography cannot be overstated, as his work represents a significant milestone in the development of modern scientific inquiry. Del Negro's detailed observations of the stars and constellations, which were described in his works, provided valuable insights into the workings of the universe, and his maps of the world helped to establish a shared understanding of the Earth's size and shape. This understanding, in turn, had a profound impact on the development of navigation, exploration, and trade, shaping the course of human history in profound ways. Despite the passing of centuries, del Negro's work remains a testament to the power of human curiosity and ingenuity, inspiring new generations of scholars and scientists to continue exploring the mysteries of the universe.

entities.summary:
Andalò del Negro (1260-1334) was a prominent Italian astronomer and geographer who played a pivotal role in the development of medieval cartography.



Del Negro's most significant contribution was his creation of the 'Carta Marina de la Mar Roja', a groundbreaking nautical map that accurately depicted the Mediterranean Sea and its surrounding lands.



This achievement not only showcased his exceptional cartographic skills but also reflected the growing interest in maritime trade and exploration during the medieval period.



Furthermore, del Negro's work in astronomy led to a greater understanding of celestial movements and the importance of astronomical observations in understanding the natural world.



His legacy can be seen in the works of later astronomers and cartographers, such as Giovanni Battista Dalle Piette, who built upon del Negro's discoveries to create even more accurate maps and astronomical models.










Andalò del Negro's significance lies in his contributions to the fields of cartography and astronomy, which had a lasting impact on the development of these disciplines during the medieval period.
